params.body:
The 419 logging that went live this morning wrote the same line five times within six minutes: the POST of the showroom screen, refused on the CSRF check. One device, a Chrome 56 kiosk on ARM, and the encrypted dealer id in the URL decrypts to **Garage Engels**.

That screen has never picked up a single change. It asks whether the car set changed, gets a refusal, and `done` never fires. Nobody was going to notice: a screen on the wall of someone else's showroom has no one watching it, and until today a 419 left no trace at all.

The showroom page is public (only `setLang`, no login) and the device hangs there for days, so it carries no usable session; our cookie is `SameSite=None` platform-wide on top of that, which a browser of that generation does not reliably keep. The question does not belong behind a CSRF check: nothing changes, the answer is "same set or not", and the dealer id is encrypted. `showroom/*` now sits in the exemptions next to `website/*`, which is there for the same reason — a form on a dealer's own domain does not carry our session either.

While in there, the older half of the same finding is closed. `check_cars()` scheduled the next check ONLY when something had changed, so after the first "no change" the screen stopped looking until the four-hourly reload. The rescheduling now hangs on `always` rather than `done`, so the watch also survives a request that never arrives — which is exactly what had been happening.

Fixes bevinding het-showroomscherm-volgt-wijzigingen-in-de-wagenset
Fixes #595
params.title: The showroom screen may ask
